gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the three headline runtimes are measured in different ways: Beatbot's 28 h is with no sun at all, Aiper's 35 h is after charging from the wall adapter, and Betta's 30+ h is per charge (one spec page says after solar charging). None turns The Hook Up's measured Aiper drain (3.46% an hour overnight with no sun) into hours. That works out to about 29 h, the same as Beatbot's no-sun claim rather than 7 h more.
standout_why: Compared against both cited pages and two uncited results. The Hook Up comparison (cited) gives drain as % per hour and 'sun hours to run continuously' (Aiper 5.7, Beatbot 6.6), but never converts the drain into hours or compares it with any maker's claim. Robotdoorstep (cited) lists 28 h and 35 h side by side as 'company claim' with no conditions, which suggests Aiper runs 25% longer. Poolbots.com (uncited result) does note the different conditions (Beatbot without sunlight, Aiper per DC charge, Betta SE Plus per charge) but converts nothing. PoolBotRanker (uncited result) lists the conditions and says nothing about Hook Up. So the different conditions show up only on uncited pages, and the conversion of the measured drain into hours appears on none.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it, and it changes how the page should say why. Measured the same way, on the battery with no sun, Aiper (about 29 h measured) and Beatbot (28 h claimed) are about equal. Aiper's 35 h only looks better because it is measured after a wall charge. For a shopper who never wants to plug in, the number that tells them apart is The Hook Up's sun hours needed to run nonstop: Aiper needs 5.7, Beatbot 6.6. That keeps Aiper as the pick for shaded pools on a like-for-like basis. One more correction: WYBOT F1's 'all day' figure is a Smart mode of 10 minutes on, 10 minutes off. That is 12 h of actual running per 24 h, and 8 h in continuous mode. Our page says WYBOT does not state the F1's runtime, which needs fixing once WYBOT's own page can be opened.

findings.label: Measured battery-only drain, converted to hours
findings.value: 3.46% per hour, about 28.9 h from full with no sun
findings.source_title: Solar Pool Skimmers – Beatbot, Aiper, & Betta vs. Generic – The Hook Up
findings.note: The Hook Up ran it overnight with no solar input and recorded battery % against time. The page calls it the most efficient skimmer tested. Arithmetic: 100 / 3.46 = 28.9 h, assuming the drain stays linear. That is about 17% below Aiper's 35 h claim, which is measured after an adapter charge.
